item.text:
**5B.1 Research Note**
Overall read: **mixed, leaning positive on the development agenda but negative on the 2024 political behavior**. Jokowi’s official economic framing was clearly growth-, poverty-, human capital-, and infrastructure-oriented, but the same year also shows substantial evidence of coalition capture, dynasty protection, and short-term influence preservation.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Indonesia Economy Projected to Remain Resilient | World Bank | 2024-06-24 | <https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/indonesia-economy-projected-to-remain-resilient> | The World Bank says Indonesia’s growth outlook is supported by public spending, business investment, and steady consumer demand, and explicitly recommends social protection, human capital, and infrastructure spending. This is strong positive evidence for a broad-based prosperity orientation. | `5B.1`, `4B.10` |
| Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: October 2024 Datasheet | World Bank | 2024-10-02 | <https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099026110152411280> | The World Bank says growth remained around 5%, poverty fell from 17.5% to 15.8% in 2024, and faster growth would require more structural reform and openness to new investment. This supports a genuine development focus, but also shows the agenda was incomplete. | `5B.1`, `4B.10` |
| Indonesia: Poverty Assessment / Growth-and-jobs findings | World Bank | 2024 | <https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs> | The World Bank says Indonesia’s growth has reduced poverty and jobs improved, but too many workers remain in low-value work and the next stage needs competition, investment, finance, and skills. This is positive evidence for sustainable prosperity rather than pure rent extraction. | `5B.1`, `4B.10` |
| Indonesia’s economy is projected to remain resilient, but reform momentum matters | AP News | 2024-02-11 | <https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-election-joko-widodo-7a47cf5e0811bedb95914b4ba20199bf> | AP framed Jokowi’s final year as a mixed record with strong growth and major infrastructure delivery, which is supportive of a prosperity-building interpretation, but also flagged dynastic concerns and a controversial capital project. | `5B.1`, `4B.10`, `4B.8` |
| Analysis-A decade of Jokowi: Indonesia’s democracy icon leaves illiberal legacy, critics say | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-10-14 | <https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/> | Reuters says Jokowi left strong growth and infrastructure, but also patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity. This is the clearest negative signal that his governing coalition was not purely aimed at broad-based sustainable prosperity. | `5B.1`, `4B.8`, `4B.5`, `4B.10` |
| Jokowi seeks Golkar takeover to retain decade-long influence | Reuters via The Jakarta Post | 2024-03-20 | <https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/03/20/jokowi-seeks-golkar-takeover-to-retain-decade-long-influence> | Reuters reported Jokowi was trying to install loyalists in Golkar and use the party as a political vehicle after office, while also protecting his legacy and family interests. This is strong evidence for loyalty-buying and influence preservation rather than purely broad-based development. | `5B.1`, `4B.8`, `4B.5` |
| ‘Jokowi effect’: How Indonesia’s outgoing leader shaped election to succeed him | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-12 | <https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/jokowi-effect-how-indonesias-outgoing-leader-shaped-election-to-succeed-him-3300317/> | Reuters said Jokowi’s son joining Prabowo’s ticket created a perceived incumbent seal of approval and shifted coalition behavior. That is negative evidence for a clean prosperity-first motive because it shows short-term political leverage was being converted into succession advantage. | `5B.1`, `4B.8`, `4B.5` |
| Indonesia shelves plan to revise election law as protests rage | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-08-22 | <https://theprint.in/world/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law/2233305/> | Reuters reported the election-law push would have helped Jokowi’s youngest son, triggered protests, and was widely read as nepotism and power consolidation. This is strong negative evidence for prioritizing loyalty and short-term family advantage over neutral, sustainable prosperity. | `5B.1`, `4B.8`, `4B.5`, `4B.10` |

**Bottom line**
- **Positive:** Jokowi’s official economic agenda in 2024 was genuinely developmental: poverty reduction, social protection, human capital, infrastructure, investment, and job-rich growth.
- **Negative:** his 2024 coalition behavior strongly suggests an additional objective of preserving political influence, rewarding loyalists, and advantaging family-linked succession paths.

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find clear direct evidence of straightforward private rent extraction in 2024.
- The stronger negative evidence is **coalition capture, patronage, and dynasty-building**, which are adjacent to rent-seeking but not identical to it.
- So the record is best read as: **developmental intent was real, but political preservation motives were also substantial**.
